sources.entry: Bolt CMS - Content Management Tool, which strives to be as simple and straightforward as possible. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Bolt is an open source PHP/Symfony content management system for building websites, usable either as a traditional CMS or headless via its API.
summary.what_it_does: Bolt is a multilingual website platform built on PHP, Symfony, Doctrine, Twig and API-Platform. It can run as a traditional CMS or as a headless/decoupled backend. Page types, fields and languages are configured in YAML. The README says it provides out-of-the-box RESTful and GraphQL APIs, a built-in editor available in 15 languages, and dummy content for testing or client demos. It also supports extensions installed from the Composer ecosystem or custom code in a project. The README lists Redactor and Article rich-content fields as part of the editor.
use_cases: Build a website with a traditional content management system
Serve content to a frontend app through a headless API
Manage page types and fields through YAML configuration
Prototype a site with dummy content before launch
how_to_run: To create a new Bolt project, follow the instructions in Bolt's distribution repository (linked from the README, commands not given in the README)
For development of Bolt CMS itself, follow the setup guide linked from the README
notable: Can be used as a traditional CMS or headless/decoupled backend
Configuration via YAML for page types, fields and languages
Editor available in 15 languages with built-in internationalisation
Includes Redactor and Article rich-content fields licensed for free use
caveats: Only the latest minor release (Bolt 6.x) is officially supported
The README says the former main maintainer died in early 2024 and new maintainers have taken over
